problem:
$$
P=[\begin{aligned}0.4 & 0.6 & 0.9 \\ 0.4 & 0.2 & 0 \\ 0.2 & 0.2 & 0.1\end{aligned}],\,q=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]
$$

Given that $q$ is the steady-state vector of the stochastic matrix $P$ shown above, what is the value of $a+b-c?$
worked_solution:
Recall that a steady-state vector of a stochastic matrix $P$ is a stochastic vector $q$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}Pq & =q \\ Pq-q & =0 \\ Pq-Iq & =0 \\ (P-I)q & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $P-I,$ we get

$$
P-I=[\begin{aligned}0.4 & 0.6 & 0.9 \\ 0.4 & 0.2 & 0 \\ 0.2 & 0.2 & 0.1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-0.6 & 0.6 & 0.9 \\ 0.4 & -0.8 & 0 \\ 0.2 & 0.2 & -0.9\end{aligned}].
$$

The matrix equation $(P-I)q=0$ is equivalent to the system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M,$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-0.6 & 0.6 & 0.9 & 0 \\ 0.4 & -0.8 & 0 & 0 \\ 0.2 & 0.2 & -0.9 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:=10{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{2}:=10{R}_{2} \\ {R}_{3}:=10{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-6 & 6 & 9 & 0 \\ 4 & -8 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 2 & -9 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}↔{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & -9 & 0 \\ 4 & -8 & 0 & 0 \\ -6 & 6 & 9 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & -9 & 0 \\ 0 & -12 & 18 & 0 \\ 0 & 12 & -18 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & -9 & 0 \\ 0 & -12 & 18 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has two pivot columns (the $1$st and $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain 

$$
{x}_{2}=\frac{3}{2}{x}_{3}.
$$

 
Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
-6{x}_{1}+6(\frac{3}{2}{x}_{3})+9{x}_{3}=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=3{x}_{3}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}3{x}_{3} \\ \frac{3}{2}{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Since the steady-state vector must be stochastic, its entries should add up to $1.$ Therefore, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}_{3}+\frac{3}{2}{x}_{3}+{x}_{3} & =1 \\ \frac{11}{2}{x}_{3} & =1 \\ {x}_{3} & =\frac{2}{11}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
q=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{6}{11} \\ \frac{3}{11} \\ \frac{2}{11}\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, 

$$
a+b-c=\frac{6}{11}+\frac{3}{11}-\frac{2}{11}=\frac{7}{11}.
$$
